title: SSH server enabled, but remote sessions are refused
scenario: A change on an isolated lab router leaves its directly connected management PC able to ping 10.8.0.1. A new SSH session is refused. The account and key configuration are unchanged, and the console remains available. The complete VTY range is 0–4.

exhibits.title: R1 VTY configuration
exhibits.text:
line vty 0 4
 login local
 transport input none

question: Which configuration is responsible for refusing new terminal sessions?
options: The unchanged host key must be regenerated for each new session.
The VTY range accepts no incoming transport despite the enabled server.
The valid local user needs a line password to supplement login local.
The active SSH configuration has to be saved before it can admit a login.
explanation: The VTY range explicitly selects transport input none; the reachable interface and enabled server do not override it. There is no evidence that the unchanged key needs replacement, and login local does not require a second shared line password. Saving the current configuration would preserve the fault rather than change active admission.
fix:
```ios R1
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# line vty 0 4
R1(config-line)# transport input ssh
R1(config-line)# end
R1# show running-config | section line vty
```
Open a new SSH session from the management PC and verify its privilege. Save after the intended access works.

title: New sessions reach authentication but no local login succeeds
scenario: After a configuration cleanup, new SSH sessions reach username/password authentication but no intended local account is accepted. The working console remains open. The administrator collects the complete username check and VTY settings below; no AAA method lists exist.

exhibits.title: Complete username check
exhibits.text:
R1# show running-config | include username
R1#

exhibits.title: R1 VTY configuration
exhibits.text:
line vty 0 4
 login local
 transport input ssh

question: Which change restores the intended named-user authentication?
options: Replace SSH with Telnet while keeping the same empty local database.
Use the enable secret as an implicit local username credential.
Create the intended local username and secret through the console.
Save the current line configuration before retrying local authentication.
explanation: The selected login local method depends on the local username database, and the complete check shows no entries. Restore the intended account through the working console, then test a new session. Changing transport, using an enable secret or saving does not create the missing login identity.
fix:
```ios R1
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# username admin privilege 15 secret AdminLabSecret8
R1(config)# end
```
Use this example secret only in the isolated lab. Verify a new SSH login, check show privilege, and save the corrected configuration.
